B. Is this measure already running in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
effect_summary_en: A Cochrane review (2022, 10 RCTs, 636 participants) found preoperative exercise cut postoperative lung complications (RR 0.45), but did not measure how many more patients became eligible for curative treatment.
supported_en: Cochrane (Granger & Cavalheri, 2022) found preoperative exercise training lowers the risk of postoperative lung complications (RR 0.45) and shortens hospital stay by about 2.2 days.
not_supported_en: No page measures how many more patients get curative-intent treatment after prehabilitation, so the assumed 0.5 percentage points (range 0–1.5) is untested.
in_use_summary_en: Tyks's lung cancer pathway page says fitness affects whether surgery is possible, but no Tyks or Varha page read mentions prehabilitation, a geriatric assessment for lung cancer patients, or reassessment before curative treatment is ruled out.
summary_en: The Tyks lung cancer pathway page says fitness and lung function decide whether surgery is possible, and that surgery is possible in about 20–25% of cases. No page read shows an exercise test, geriatric assessment or prehabilitation at Tyks or Varha. A similar preoperative model has been described only for Pirkanmaa and the Tays area. A 2022 Cochrane review found exercise before lung surgery cuts lung complications (RR 0.45), but it does not show that more patients become eligible for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: I found no Varha or Tyks page on prehabilitation or geriatric assessment for lung cancer, and no study measuring the rise in curative-intent treatment.
